name: Fairchild Hall
use: Traditional-style residence hall, 125 students; International Connections theme hall and Honors RLC (3rd floor)

renovations.what: Complete renovation; began housing international students in 2010
Fairchild-Huddleston courtyard rebuilt ($508,000): new concrete, single staircase with code-height steel railings, lighting, landscaping

facts.text: Dedicated April 12, 1916 and named for Edward T. Fairchild, New Hampshire College president 1912-1917, whose tenure saw three dormitories and DeMeritt Hall built.
Completely renovated in 2008; it began housing international students in 2010.
Home of the International Connections themed hall and an Honors community; rooms come in unique sizes with large windows facing Main Street.
Has air conditioning and an elevator; roll-in access to the building is by the elevator only. Address 67 Main St.; 125 students.
The rusted, non-code stairs in the courtyard it shares with Huddleston Hall were replaced in fall 2025.

tnh_court.title: Fairchild, Huddleston courtyard renovation addressing safety concerns nears completion

verdict: 1916 brick hall on Main Street, fully renovated in 2008 with A/C and an elevator; home of the international community.
notes: No licensed photo found: Commons search by name and the UNH category crawl found nothing for Fairchild, and Flickr could not be searched without an API key. The archives reference photo is a historic black-and-white view: a three-and-a-half-storey brick block with a central entrance, gabled ends and chimneys. Architect and style unconfirmed (old row said 'not Huddleston'; I found no source either way). Old row's 2008 cost (~$8.5M, ACUHO award), room mix and the Roomsurf 'hotel' quote were not re-verified. Natural light 'strong' rests on Housing's 'large windows' description only.
judgeNotes: Only a historic archives photo (plain three-and-a-half-storey block). Each score down about a point from the old run for lack of evidence. Condition 7: the 2008 renovation is now 18 years old.
